inputs.proposal: J2534 request modes: the set scheduler owns requests whenever the profile has mux defs, ?poll= is rejected at parse time unless ?filter= gives it a channel, and the single-PID poll request is built on the first channel.
inputs.original_proposal: J2534 request modes: the set scheduler owns requests whenever the profile has mux defs, ?poll= is rejected at parse time unless ?filter= gives it a channel, and the single-PID poll request is built on the first channel.

blockers: claim: Critical logic error: worker function incorrectly sets sched_mode without checking poll_pid, causing scheduler to override single-PID poll; file: core/src/j2534_transport.cpp; quote: const bool sched_mode = (t->sched.count > 0);

claim: Logic error: channel selection for poll requests changed from dynamic lookup to hardcoded channel 0, ignoring PID-specific channel routing; file: core/src/j2534_transport.cpp; quote: build_mode01_request(req, t->chans[0].tx_id, t->poll_pid);
questions: Is there thread safety protection for t->poll_pid access in the worker thread? No mutexes visible in the shown code.
What is the actual buffer size requirement for Mode 01 requests? The code uses uint8_t req[6], but CAN-FD support may require larger buffers.
How does rx_for_pid() work with the set scheduler? The removed code shows it was used to route PIDs to channels.
What is the relationship between poll_pid and the set scheduler? The proposal says scheduler 'owns requests' when profile has mux defs.
Is there a race condition if poll_pid is modified while the worker thread is running?
nits: Comment in SettingsPage.qml mentions 'the scheduler owns requests' but the implementation allows poll to override scheduler when sched.count == 0
Removed comments in parse_query explained the original design intent - the new check breaks that design
The struct qttune_j2534_uri_params should document that rx_id == 0 means 'use profile's channels' per the struct comment
